format: CSV tables and one JSON file per collected host

files.collection.json: host, ip, os, collected_utc, collected_by, tool, case, logon_history_window_days, items (rows and SHA-256 of each table), samples (placeholder files)
files.file_listing.csv: path, size_bytes, created_utc, modified_utc, sha256, signer
files.autoruns.csv: location (service, registry run key, scheduled task), name, image_path, signer, sha256, enabled, first_seen_utc
files.services.csv: name, display_name, start_type, state, image_path, account, installed_utc
files.scheduled_tasks.csv: task_name, action, author, created_utc, last_run_utc, trigger
files.logon_history.csv: time_utc, event_id (4624, 4625, 4634, 4647), user, domain, logon_type, src_ip, logon_id; the 45 days before the collection
files.network_config.csv: interface, ip, mac, gateway, dns_servers, dhcp_enabled
files.placeholders/<name>.placeholder.txt: inert text stand-in for an unsigned executable the collector copied (every collection has some: in-house utilities, vendor tools, downloaded programs); its SHA-256 is the hash the logs record for that file

notes: Fourteen collections taken by the utility's security team between 2027-10-02 and 2027-10-14. Listings and hashes only: no executable content is included anywhere. The tables agree with the Windows event logs and the endpoint telemetry of the same host. Times are UTC. No time in a collection is later than the collection.
